answer: Each agent may submit one claim per epoch, but a claim earns transferable credits only after a randomly selected peer verifies it and stakes credits of their own; false claims forfeit that stake. A newcomer therefore cannot multiply influence just by minting identities: each identity needs scarce credits and independent endorsers, while colluding endorsers risk losing their own stake. An attacker must acquire credits, recruit trustworthy peers, and keep capital locked up, making a marble, copper, or walnut-sized fake network costly to scale.
